text:
emma (support): FYI we've got a customer report: requests keep getting routed to eu-west-1 even though their client explicitly sets region=us-east-1 in the query string. high p99 and cross-region egress costs. attaching minimal repro and logs they pasted.

customer: curl -v "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?region=us-east-1" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_xxx" -H "X-Origin-Region: eu-west-1"

customer (logs): request_id=abc123 route_decision=eu-west-1 backend=eu-west-1 latency_ms=820
customer: we don't set X-Origin-Region, our infra (cdn) injects it for geo routing, but it conflicts with the query param. can you confirm which you use?

emma (support): thanks — can you paste full request headers and the exact timestamp? also which SDK/version? I'll escalate if needed. :eyes:

raj (infra): looking now. quick hypothesis: our router currently prefers the X-Origin-Region header if present. that was added to allow internal region pinning via reverse-proxy. if a client CDN injects a different value we're seeing misroutes.

kai (eng): confirming. current routing precedence (simplified):
```
if (headers['X-Origin-Region']) {
  target = resolve_region(headers['X-Origin-Region'])
} else if (query['region']) {
  target = resolve_region(query['region'])
} else {
  target = geo_lookup(client_ip)
}
```
This was intentional for partner internal traffic but is causing customer-visible misroutes when external CDNs inject the header.

sarah (product): this explains the cost spike ticket. customer expects query param to serve as authoritative override. we should avoid changing semantics customer-facing without notice.

tim (oncall): we've seen a similar loop yesterday where fallback policy caused repeated cross-region retries: gateway picks eu for incoming header, fails quota check, then fallback tries us-east but the CDN re-adds header on the retry -> routed back to eu -> loop. logs show alternating route_decision values and identical request IDs with retry_count increments.

ops-bot: Incident flagged: INC-2026-042 — tagging infra and product teams.

emma (support): proposed immediate mitigations?

raj (infra): short-term: add a safeguard to ignore X-Origin-Region if the source IP is not in our trusted proxy list. quick ACL check before honoring header. can be rolled in ~30–45m, no deploy required if we toggle config.

kai (eng): mid-term: change precedence so client-supplied query param overrides header from untrusted sources. we should also canonicalize header names to avoid CDN variants (X-Client-Region, X-Origin-Region, X-Geo).

sarah (product): long-term: publish a compatibility note and update SDKs to avoid injecting region headers unless explicitly configured. also add a console warning for customers using query region param when a conflicting header is detected.

emma (support): asked customer to remove/strip the header on their CDN as a temporary workaround and provided this command for repro:

```
# verify header isn't added by CDN
curl -I -s -D - https://edge-check.example/ --resolve api.redwood.example:443:IP
```

customer: i removed the header at CDN edge, routing now respects region=us-east-1 and p99 dropped to 120ms. thanks.

kai (eng): follow-ups for the backlog:
- (ENG-1129) change routing precedence: prefer explicit query param over headers from non-private sources
- (ENG-1130) add header canonicalization + whitelist of trusted proxies
- (ENG-1131) add dashboard alert for when routing decision disagrees with client-specified region

tim (oncall): note — watch for any regressions in next 24h, will monitor INC-2026-042. if we see retries/loops re-open immediately.

emma (support): closing loop with customer and documenting steps. closing thread when incident is resolved. :white_check_mark:
